Scenario Context: Routine maintenance at 20ft using hand tools.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Good assessment. Tools tethered at height prevent fatal dropped-object hazards.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: tethered tools control the dropped-object risk. Swipe right and approve operations when the stated controls are in place.

Scenario Context: Final visual sweep before aircraft pushback.
Wrong 1: Ignore it, it is a small item
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: You stopped a hazard! Loose hardware and rags are critical FOD that can puncture tires or be ingested.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Loose hardware and rags create foreign-object debris (FOD). Swipe left, halt the activity and clear the debris.

Scenario Context: Scaffolding platform during a shift change.
Wrong 1: Leave it for the next shift
Wrong 2: Throw it down to the ground worker
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Look closer next time! Unsecured tools on ledges are prime drop hazards for workers below.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. A tool left unsecured on a platform edge can fall onto people below. Swipe left and secure the tool before work continues.

Scenario Context: End-of-shift tool inventory.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Perfect. Shadowed toolboxes make it easy to assess that no tools were left behind as FOD.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: the shadowed toolbox supports a complete tool inventory. Swipe right and approve operations after confirming every tool is accounted for.

Scenario Context: Installation of overhead fixtures.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Open buckets at height vibrate. Bolts can easily fall, becoming both a strike hazard and ground FOD.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Loose bolts in an open bucket can fall from height. Swipe left and use the specified zippered pouch to contain them.

Scenario Context: Performing inspection near an unguarded drop.
Wrong 2: Hold their legs while they work
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Wearing a harness isn't enough. You must assess if they are actually tied off to an anchor point.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. A harness alone does not provide protection if it is not connected to an appropriate anchor. Swipe left and enforce the required tie-off before work continues.

Scenario Context: Transporting materials to the upper deck.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Stop! Workers must maintain three points of contact on a ladder. Materials should be hoisted separately.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Carrying materials while climbing prevents the worker from maintaining three points of contact. Swipe left and use the specified hoist or rope for the materials.

Scenario Context: Bringing tools up to the roof level.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Excellent management. Tools are secured during transit and the worker is safe.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: tools are secured during transport to roof level. Swipe right and approve operations while maintaining those controls.

Scenario Context: Floor condition after a wiring job.
Wrong 1: Leave it for the cleaners tonight
Wrong 2: Blow it away with compressed air
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Small clippings are dangerous FOD. Always manage your workspace and clean as you go.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Wiring clippings left on the floor create FOD. Swipe left and sweep the area rather than leaving or blowing the debris elsewhere.

Scenario Context: Ground level below active overhead work.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Good look! Barricading the area below manages the risk of dropped objects hitting personnel.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: barricades keep people out of the area beneath overhead work. Swipe right and approve operations while the exclusion area remains controlled.

Scenario Context: Reaching a high ceiling fixture.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Never stand on the top step. Assess the height required and get the proper equipment for the job.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Standing on the top step is unsafe. Swipe left and obtain a suitable taller ladder instead of improvising extra height.

Scenario Context: Technician took a quick lunch break.
Wrong 2: Push them further back on the wing
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Stop operations! Items left on aircraft surfaces are critical FOD if forgotten before flight.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Items left on an aircraft surface can become FOD if forgotten. Swipe left and remove the items before operations resume.

Scenario Context: Routine tarmac maintenance.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Active FOD management is crucial. Routine sweeping keeps the operations area safe.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: routine sweeping controls FOD in the operations area. Swipe right and approve operations while keeping the area clear.

Scenario Context: Digital inspection on an elevated platform.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Great assessment. Even digital devices must be tethered when working at heights.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: the digital device is tethered during work at height. Swipe right and approve operations while the tether remains secure.

Scenario Context: Quick adjustment on the hangar floor.
Wrong 2: Hold the bucket steady for them
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Buckets are not approved working platforms. They can easily collapse or slip.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. A bucket is not a suitable working platform and may slip or collapse. Swipe left and provide a proper step stool.

Scenario Context: Waste management setup.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Covered bins manage FOD by preventing wind from blowing trash back onto the tarmac.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: covered bins prevent wind from spreading waste onto the tarmac. Swipe right and approve operations while the bins remain closed.

Scenario Context: Windy conditions during outdoor ops.
Wrong 1: Wait for the wind to stop
Wrong 2: Assume it will blow off the runway
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Personal items are FOD too! Assess weather conditions and secure loose clothing/hats.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. A loose personal item in windy conditions can become FOD. Swipe left and arrange safe retrieval under local operating procedures, then secure loose items.

Scenario Context: Long-term construction structure.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Toe-boards are a great management tool. They prevent kicks and stops loose tools from falling off the edge.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: toe-boards help stop loose tools from falling off the platform. Swipe right and approve operations while these controls remain in place.

Scenario Context: Post-maintenance ceiling inspection.
Wrong 1: Leave it, it is secure in the rafters
Wrong 2: Log it as lost and forget about it
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Hidden tools are ticking time bombs. Always do a final look and tool count after high-altitude work.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. A tool left in the rafters can become a falling-object hazard. Swipe left and arrange safe retrieval, then complete the tool count.

Scenario Context: Climbing structural steel.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Excellent. Closed tool pouches manage the risk of items slipping out during complex movements.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: closed tool pouches help keep tools secure during climbing. Swipe right and approve operations while tools remain contained.

Scenario Context: Setting up a temporary projector for a meeting.
Management Action: Tape down or use a cable cover
Correct Action: Tape down or use a cable cover
Wrong 1: Warn people to step over it
Wrong 2: Unplug it and leave it there
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Stop and look at walkways. Unsecured cords are major trip hazards in office environments.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. An unsecured cord across a walkway creates a trip hazard. Swipe left and secure it with the specified tape or cable cover.

Scenario Context: Employee needing more outlets for personal devices.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Daisy-chaining power strips is a severe fire hazard. Assess electrical needs and manage through Facilities.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Daisy-chained power strips create a fire hazard. Swipe left, stop using the arrangement and request a suitable electrical solution through Facilities.

Scenario Context: Recent office supply delivery left in the hallway.
Wrong 1: Put a sign on the boxes
Wrong 2: Wait for the supply team to move them
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Never block emergency equipment. Assess delivery placements to manage emergency readiness.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Boxes obstruct access to emergency equipment. Swipe left and relocate them to keep that access clear.

Scenario Context: Recent spill that was just mopped up.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Great management! Identifying spills and using proper signage prevents serious slip and fall injuries.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: the spill has been addressed and warning signage is in place. Swipe right and approve operations while managing any remaining slip risk.

Scenario Context: Running out of storage space in a cubicle.
Management Action: Move heavy items to bottom shelves
Correct Action: Move heavy items to bottom shelves
Wrong 1: Push them further back on the top shelf
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Look up! Heavy objects stored high up are dangerous falling hazards in an office setting.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Heavy items stored high up can fall and cause injury. Swipe left and move them to suitable lower shelves.

Scenario Context: Employee walked away to answer a phone call.
Wrong 1: Put a warning cone next to it
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Always manage your workspace. Open drawers are frequent causes of tripping and severe shin injuries.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. An open drawer creates a trip and impact hazard. Swipe left and close the drawer.

Scenario Context: Relaxing during a long conference call.
Management Action: Keep all wheels on the floor
Correct Action: Keep all wheels on the floor
Wrong 2: Put feet on the desk to balance
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Stop risky behavior. Office chairs are not designed to tilt like this and can easily tip over backward.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. Tilting the office chair risks a backward fall. Swipe left and keep all wheels on the floor.

Scenario Context: A newly set up ergonomic workstation.
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Excellent hazard management. Proper cable routing prevents trips, snags, and equipment damage.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: This scenario is marked safe: the workstation has proper cable routing. Swipe right and approve operations while keeping cables clear of walking areas.

Scenario Context: Disposing of confidential documents in the copy room.
Management Action: Tuck in or remove the tie
Correct Action: Tuck in or remove the tie
Wrong 2: Hold the tie with one hand
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Look at what you are wearing. Loose clothing or lanyards can easily get pulled into moving office machinery.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. A loose tie can become caught in the shredder. Swipe left and tuck in or remove the tie before using the machine.

Scenario Context: Left unattended after assembling a presentation.
Wrong 1: Put a sticky note on it saying Sharp
Wrong 2: Leave it open for the next person
SLAM Feedback: SLAM: Always assess shared tools. Leaving sharp blades exposed is a critical laceration risk for the next user.
Incorrect Swipe Feedback: Do not approve this scenario. An unattended raised cutter blade exposes the next user to injury. Swipe left and lower and lock the blade.
